topology: PC1–R1–R2–R3–SRV1, with prepared IPv4 addressing and HTTP. AS100 uses MD5 on every routed transit, key7 and EnarsiAuth7 under locally named EDGE-A/TRANSIT/EDGE-C chains. R1/R2 forms a working control adjacency and advertises R2 Loopback0 198.51.100.2/32. Practice starts with passive R3 Gi0/1 plus WrongAuth7 on R3 key7.
implemented: Twelfth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies catalog entry with independently instantiated practice/completed documents, five-row plan, staged diagnostic guide, tested CLI references and current-domain/path/query share links. Existing entries remain; ENCOR39 and ENCOR Layer3 nine are preserved.

Initial diagnosis requires three real server probes dropped for No route at R1 plus three accepted/delivered R2-loopback control replies while physical links and R1/R2 adjacency stay up. Show commands or fewer probes cannot earn this goal. Fixing only passive policy or only the key string cannot restore R2/R3.

Live checks enforce classic AS100, exact networks, router IDs, passive LANs and active transits, default K-values, all configured local MD5 bindings and matching key7/material. Different key-chain names are intentional. Removing authentication can allow forwarding but fails secure policy, health and repair grading.

R1/R3 install opposite LANs as internal D routes at AD90/classic metric10240; R2 installs both remote LANs at7680. CEF next hops/interfaces and all four directional UP neighbors are checked. Matching authentication alone does not install a route before the actual EIGRP UPDATE is delivered.

Both host directions require three accepted requests and parent-linked delivered replies across the real R1/R2/R3 egresses. HTTP requires an actual complete200 response with the exact expected service body through R2. A wrong200 page, show-only output or a successful transport alone is insufficient.

Five separate controlled faults exercise wrong key string, key9 replacing key7 with unchanged material, a binding to missing chain MISSING, passive transit and mismatched K-values. Each needs the correct fault configuration, missing R3 adjacency/server routes, three No route server failures, three successful control replies, restoration and fresh three replies in both host directions.

Configuration-only toggles, two failed probes, server power loss, static shortcuts, rewiring or unrelated outages cannot impersonate the specific incidents. Independent historical observations do not replace live health. Unsaved configuration revokes the save goal.

Six live and eight observed criteria yield practice0/14, diagnosed1/14, repaired baseline9/14 and full14/14. The completed reference supplies only six live goals without invented initial diagnosis, traffic, service or recovery history.

Per-attempt config/route epochs and normal simulator notifications capture actual CLI/traffic evidence with the guide closed. YAML export/import retains earned observations while protocol/transport caches rebuild. A fresh practice resets all history. Canonical config replays into clean routers; saved reload restores an unsaved wrong key.

No simulation engine, protocol transport, CLI parser, UI styling, terminal colors/fonts/controls or artwork changed. The lab uses working existing features and follows Cisco IOS reference behavior within documented simulator limits.
scope: Classic IOS EIGRP for IPv4 neighbor eligibility and MD5/key-chain configuration troubleshooting. Authentication eligibility currently compares active key IDs and material in the computed control-plane model; this is not a fresh CML capture, wire-driven cryptographic MD5 implementation, IOS binary compatibility or exact Cisco authentication debug/timer emulation. NX-OS, named/IPv6 authentication, HMAC-SHA-256, multi-key rollover and timed send/accept-lifetime exercises are not advertised by this lab. Keys use no explicit lifetimes; native validation also rejects expired-key drift. See docs/audits/eigrp-update-fidelity.md for existing engine limits.
